data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["A WAL has explicit checkpoint records; token-budget exhaustion may not leave a marker.","Database recovery can replay; append-only reasoning logs must not replay.","Model state is probabilistic and harder to fingerprint than deterministic computation."],"overturn_conditions":["If events are self-describing and causally linked by content hash, even a logical mid-unit stop preserves identity because the next event simply references the last complete one.","If the system supports partial-event resumption (streaming append), the mid-write case may be safe under a different protocol."],"shared_structure":["A checkpointed process interrupted by external resource exhaustion (token budget \u2248 CPU time limit).","Resume requires a valid checkpoint marker and unchanged environment.","Append-only log \u2248 write-ahead log (WAL) in databases."],"source_memory_refs":["SRC_001"],"transfer_claims":["The WAL discipline of 'never overwrite, only append' transfers directly: resumption is safe iff the last committed record is complete.","The 'fuzzy checkpoint' problem transfers: if the checkpoint is ambiguous, recovery must be conservative."]},"claim":"Resumption is safe if and only if the last recorded event in the log is well-formed and complete, and the causal preconditions (program, inputs, model-state checkpoint) are demonstrably unchanged at resumption time. The append-only identity is preserved because new events extend the same causal chain without rewriting any prior event.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the last event is partial or malformed (interrupted mid-write), resumption cannot locate a valid causal parent and must be refused.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the program, input, or model checkpoint has changed since the run started, the causal fingerprint mismatches and resumed events would not belong to the same causal chain.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the event-log format lacks a content-addressable hash linking events, there is no mechanism to verify causal continuity on resumption.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"An event log maintains append-only identity through a causal chain: each event references its predecessor. Token-budget exhaustion is an external interrupt, not a logical termination. If the interrupt fell between complete events (not mid-write), the last event's hash serves as a resume cursor. The resumption process reads this cursor, verifies the program/input/model fingerprint matches, and appends new events that reference the last committed event as their causal parent. No rewrite occurs, so append-only identity is intact.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
